pending_interview.category: System design (general) — scalability patterns; designing common systems like a URL shortener, rate limiter, chat system, notification system
pending_interview.question: You are asked to design a rate limiter — a system that prevents any single user or client from making too many requests to an API in a given time window. Walk through your design. How does the system know how many requests a given user has made recently? Where does that state live, and why? How does your design behave when the system is under extremely high traffic? What are the tradeoffs between being strict (never allowing a single extra request) versus approximate (allowing slightly over the limit occasionally in exchange for better performance and simpler design)?
